name: Diego S. Maranan
half:
Diego S. Maranan has advised three theses in this repository between 2022 and 2023. Their supervision covers diverse areas including online and distance learning, arts and creative practice, culture and identity, information systems, and business and entrepreneurship. Specific advised works include studies on Mayer's Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning in MOOC experiences, an autoethnographic study of the shift from textserye to novel-type books, and the viability of digital artwork as NFTs in multimedia.

Their own research output is extensive, with 47 articles in this repository and the latest item dated 2026. Their research focus is heavily centered on arts and creative practice, which appears in 29 of their items. Other significant research interests include futures and philosophy (11 items), information systems (10 items), online and distance learning (5 items), culture and identity (4 items), management and leadership (4 items), climate and disaster (3 items), educational technology (3 items), language and literacy (2 items), and nursing and patient care (2 items). Their work frequently explores the intersections of artscience, speculative design, and somaesthetics, often within the context of the Global South. They have also published on topics such as digital transformation in higher education, wearable technologies, and the integration of arts into transdisciplinary research. Evidence of their research breadth is shown through their engagement with diverse fields ranging from blockchain technology to aerospace medicine.

A recurring theme in Maranan's work is the intersection of art, technology, and somatic experience. They have published extensively on "artscience," exploring how collaborative art can facilitate idea generation and transdisciplinary research. Their work often investigates how technology can be designed for body awareness, specifically through vibrotactile stimulation and somaesthetic technology, as seen in their Haplós project. They have also explored speculative design and futures thinking, particularly in the context of the Global South, addressing topics such as space settlement ideology, wearable technologies, and the intersection of art and science in the Philippines.

Maranan's interest in digital transformation and educational technology is evident in their work on Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), digital transformation in higher education, and the use of collaborative relational database Software-as-a-Service for learning management systems. They have also addressed management and leadership through studies on faculty recruitment in Open and Distance e-Learning (ODeL) environments and the evaluation of collaborative research projects. Additionally, they have explored environmental and social issues through creative responses to sustainability and multispecies proposals for climate impact. Their work touches on various media, from new media art and immersive installations to the mapping of the Philippine moving image. While their recent repository activity includes items dated up to 2026, they have no advisees listed for the year 2026.
